A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WorldLens research and contain 80 readable pages, including the complete appendices. Text comparison and page rendering support a reliable comparison of the scientific content and presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original driving-world-model evaluations, human-preference measurements, and WorldLens-Agent assessments in Section 5 and the appendices, including Tables 1–29.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark experiments, human-preference results, and evaluation-agent assessments.

M1.justification: The WorldLens evaluation framework and WorldLens-Agent procedure are unchanged, including Qwen3-VL-8B, attention-layer LoRA adaptation, frozen components, and score-and-rationale outputs.

E1.justification: The same five evaluation aspects and data coverage are retained, including nuScenes, WorldLens-26K, and the appendix's Gen3C, Cosmos-Drive, and CARLA examples. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the corresponding main and appendix tables. This includes both the six-model Generation/Reconstruction comparisons and the distinct Action-Following comparator set in Table 2.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, preprocessing, validation data, simulation settings, reconstruction budgets, human-rating procedures, and agent training configurations are unchanged. For example, Section 9.1.3 retains the 150-scene nuScenes validation set and one-second planning horizon.

E4.justification: The same good/bad examples, failure illustrations, and out-of-distribution WorldLens-Agent case studies remain, including Figures 8, 36, and 37. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 24–29 retain identical reporting of means, standard deviations, medians, quartiles, and extrema for human ratings. No repeated-run information, uncertainty estimation, or significance-testing practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–29 and the reported qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains DiST-4D's Perceptual Discrepancy of 58.08 and OpenDWM's Photometric Error of 0.065. Raster changes preserve the illustrated examples.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and metric formulations in Appendix Sections 7–10, including Equations 1–22, are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: WorldLens, WorldLens-26K, and WorldLens-Agent. Claims about complementary evaluation dimensions and the absence of a universally dominant model are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 retains the same interpretations of geometry, appearance, and downstream utility. Section 13.3 retains the same limitations concerning driving-domain scope, annotator bias, inherited agent limitations, and evolving physical-realism criteria.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, and resource-access information are unchanged. Section 12.3 still specifies LoRA rank 16, three training epochs, and eight A100 GPUs; project, code, and dataset links are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and the positioning against prior evaluation and world-model research are identical. No cited work or novelty claim is added or removed.

P1.justification: Section 4.2 changes '(section 3.5)' to '(see Section 3.5)', and the first-page arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining wording and document organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Some graphics in Figures 4, 21, 22, and 24 are re-encoded or resampled; for example, Figure 21's trajectory panels decrease from 2000×2000 to 1200×1200 pixels. Their content, captions, and placement remain unchanged. Section 4.2 also has minor line reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the methods, empirical evidence, mathematical content, reproducibility information, and limitations of v1. The cross-reference edit and small raster-presentation changes neither resolve a substantive deficiency nor materially impair readability or evidential support.
